AW-STUDY-0047

Rigged Hero Cut-Out

Evan pasted a flying hero and asked for a fully rigged skeleton with decorations, so stock 2D bipedal animations can drive it. We cut the picture into 16 body parts and 3 decorations, hung them on 16 named bones, and exported a Unity-style package. The rig turns correctly in our test renders. I could not run Unity here, so the Unity builder script is untested.

The parts

The rig turning

What is in the package

  • rig.json: bones (parent, pivot, tip), parts (sprite file, bone, draw order), decorations flagged. Bone names follow the Character Studio set, with the character's own sides: hips, spine, neck, head, upperarm/forearm/hand_L/R, thigh/shin/foot_L/R.
  • sprites/: 19 transparent PNGs. poses.json: the four poses as local rotations per bone, ready to key.
  • unity/AwRigBuilder.cs: an editor menu that builds a prefab (bone GameObjects with SpriteRenderers sorted by draw order) from the rig. Any stock clip that rotates those bone paths then plays on it.

How to use it in Unity

  1. Copy the study folder (rig.json, sprites, unity) under Assets, keep AwRigBuilder.cs in an Editor folder.
  2. Menu Abbie's World, Build 2D Rig From rig.json, and pick rig.json.
  3. Drag the prefab into a scene; make clips that rotate the bone transforms, or retarget a stock set to the same bone names.

Honest limits

  • Unity untested. The script is written to the Unity 2021 API but never compiled or run.
  • Rigid parts, not a mesh skin. Parts rotate like paper cut-outs; elbows and knees show a seam when bent far. Unity's 2D Animation package (sprite mesh skinning) would blend them, and needs a layered PSB.
  • Hidden areas are missing. Where one limb covered another, nothing was ever drawn behind it, so big turns show gaps. The hair and belt cut-outs left smeary fill on the head and chest.
  • The hero is front-facing. Most stock 2D clips are side views, so a walk or run on this picture reads oddly. A side or neutral three-quarter view would take stock clips better.
  • Our web engine uses its own 2D rig format; the same bones and parts load there too if we want to skip Unity.

Even better if

  1. Midjourney drew the hero as a rest-pose turnaround (front, side, back) with arms down and no overlaps, so every part is fully visible.
  2. Each part were painted complete (the hidden half of every limb) before rigging.
  3. Limbs became soft meshes with weights at the joints instead of rigid pieces.
  4. A real Unity test, with one stock walk cycle retargeted, before we call this finished.

Code: tools/rig-cutout/ (cutout.py, pose.py, example/). Picture: pasted by Evan. Tour: no.
